content.text: I was very easily able to replicate the transaction database entries persisting through restarts (and never going away), but I’m having a hard to replicating the transactions not rolling back after timing out.
I have been testing with
mvn jetty:run
and postgres running in docker using the instructions from:
Its possible I replicated this at some point, but I think it might be getting confounded by weirdness with the expiration times. The
Atomic-Expires

header when doing a GET against a TX is returning values that don’t seem to match my config. Like I configured it to expire in 60 seconds, and it seemed to take about 3 minutes, and then i configured 2 minutes and the
Atomic-Expires

was about 5-6 minutes in the future, and the database entries finally cleared about 7-8 minutes after the last request made to the tx. I also removed the config so that it’d default to 3 minutes, and it took about 7 minutes to expire.
I wanted to note that I also don’t see any entries in the
containment_transactions
search_resource_rdf_type_transactions
, or
simple_search_transactions

tables if I just create a transaction and don’t make any changes. As far as I can tell there isn’t a representation of the transaction on its own. So it would make sense that we only see stuff left over after making changes in the TX. Unless there is some sort of postgres internal transactions table you were referring to?
Just recording my steps here:
Started fcrepo with:
MAVEN_OPTS='-Dfcrepo.config.file=/path/to/test-config.properties' mvn jetty:run -pl fcrepo-webapp
where the properties file configures fedora to use postgres based the instructions on that page. I also tried various transaction timeout values.
I then started a transaction and used it to create a container and check the expiration time.

curl -i -X POST "http://localhost:8080/rest/fcr:tx" -ufedoraAdmin:fedoraAdmin
curl -H"Atomic-ID: http://localhost:8080/rest/fcr:tx/9e0bfafc-94a1-4178-976c-27998f279937" -X POST "http://localhost:8080/rest/test_container" -H"Slug: newone" -ufedoraAdmin:fedoraAdmin
curl -i -X GET "http://localhost:8080/rest/fcr:tx/9e0bfafc-94a1-4178-976c-27998f279937" -ufedoraAdmin:fedoraAdmin
Connected to the database and queried the transaction tables:
I then waited for the transaction to timeout.

As described above, the entries seem to get cleared if I wait until after the Atomic Expires value returned in a GET request to the TX URI. But the amount of time before it expires seems a lot longer than the time i configured.

I tried methodically trying various conditions, but never ended up with transaction entries that stuck around forever except when I restarted fedora with transactions still live. Recording the approaches tried:
Starting TX, creating a new container, then waiting 3 minutes (have it configured to 60s but it seems to be taking 3 minutes)
rolls back and clears DB
After letting a tx roll back without restarting anything, start tx, create new container with same name, wait 3 minutes
rolls back and clears DB
Without restarting, start tx, make GET requests against TX to check exp, create container, make GET requests against TX
rolls back after the updated tx exp time
Create a container outside tx, make a tx, create a container in the tx (not in the outside container)
rolls back after the tx exp time
Make a tx, create a container in a basic container that existed before the tx
rolls back after the tx exp time
Make a tx, create a container in an existing basic container, manually roll back, make another tx, create container again
rolls back after about 2 minutes
Make a tx, create a container in an existing basic container, shut down fedora, start fedora back up
tx entries still in db
GET for the tx returns 404, DELETE to tx returns 404
7b. With tx table containing stale entry from before restart, make a tx, create a container
rolls back, and cleans up the new tx entries (the old ones stay)
Restart postgres and fcrepo, make a tx, create a container
rolls back, cleans up the new tx entries
Restart fcrepo (but not postgres), make a tx, create a container
rolls back, cleans up the new tx entries
Change fcrepo timeout to 2 minutes, make a tx, create a container, GET request to check exp time
rolls back, cleans up tx entries after about 7-8 minutes
2 min timeout, Make tx, create container, use GET to check Atomic Expires and compare to DB
Atomic-Expires 19:01:01 GMT, start time in DB 14:55:16, so almost 6 minutes
after 2 minutes, GET to tx still says its active
at :01:01 mark, GET returns 410 and the db entries are gone
Remove timeout config, make tx, create container
Atomic expires 19:13:04 GMT, start time in DB 15:04:25, so close to 7 minutes
GET still active after 3mins
Reports 410 and db entries removed after the atomic expires value
The problem with transactions after reboot is in another issue:

As for remaining transactions without restart, in our case the transaction gets stuck permanently and no rollback occurs at all. We have left the default value in the configuration. Also, I'll just explicitly point out that we're working with version 6.4 - if you were testing on 6.5, it might be different.

As for opening the transaction without further changes, I honestly don't know how it is represented. But I have tested its closure by checking that if I waited more than 3 min (approximately) after opening a transaction to send additional content, Fedora returned the information that the transaction did not exist.

If it would help, I can send some more information about our instance or the procedure, but there is nothing particularly special about them. Transactions remain stuck sometimes for a single action, sometimes for a series of actions - it doesn't seem to matter.
Hopefully this PR should either help with or resolve the issue:

The expiration times of transactions were having the timeout period added to them every request rather than being set to the now+timeout. The result was that if you made a lot of requests in a transaction, each one would add 3 minutes to the expiration time. For example, making 100 requests (read or write) gives you an expiration time 300min after the transaction was started. So it could effectively produce transactions that never seem to timeout.
Resolved with
https://github.com/fcrepo/fcrepo/commit/dc4040691a3540ba8d997cf66a798b6ad3ac96bf
During testing, we encounter the problem that the automatic transaction rollback (

) is not applied if at least one reuqest has been sent to the transaction. In this case, the transaction remains uncommitted until the manual rollback is performed. If transaction is empty it is correctly rolled back after the period set in the config file.

comments.body:
I was very easily able to replicate the transaction database entries persisting through restarts (and never going away), but I’m having a hard to replicating the transactions not rolling back after timing out.

I have been testing with mvn jetty:run and postgres running in docker using the instructions from:

https://wiki.lyrasis.org/display/FEDORA6x/Database+Cache#DatabaseCache-PostgreSQL.2

Its possible I replicated this at some point, but I think it might be getting confounded by weirdness with the expiration times. The Atomic-Expires header when doing a GET against a TX is returning values that don’t seem to match my config. Like I configured it to expire in 60 seconds, and it seemed to take about 3 minutes, and then i configured 2 minutes and the Atomic-Expires was about 5-6 minutes in the future, and the database entries finally cleared about 7-8 minutes after the last request made to the tx. I also removed the config so that it’d default to 3 minutes, and it took about 7 minutes to expire.

I wanted to note that I also don’t see any entries in the containment_transactions, search_resource_rdf_type_transactions, or simple_search_transactions tables if I just create a transaction and don’t make any changes. As far as I can tell there isn’t a representation of the transaction on its own. So it would make sense that we only see stuff left over after making changes in the TX. Unless there is some sort of postgres internal transactions table you were referring to?

Just recording my steps here:

Started fcrepo with:

MAVEN_OPTS='-Dfcrepo.config.file=/path/to/test-config.properties' mvn jetty:run -pl fcrepo-webapp

where the properties file configures fedora to use postgres based the instructions on that page. I also tried various transaction timeout values.

I then started a transaction and used it to create a container and check the expiration time.

curl -i -X POST "http://localhost:8080/rest/fcr:tx" -ufedoraAdmin:fedoraAdmin
curl -H"Atomic-ID: http://localhost:8080/rest/fcr:tx/9e0bfafc-94a1-4178-976c-27998f279937" -X POST "http://localhost:8080/rest/test_container" -H"Slug: newone" -ufedoraAdmin:fedoraAdmin
curl -i -X GET "http://localhost:8080/rest/fcr:tx/9e0bfafc-94a1-4178-976c-27998f279937" -ufedoraAdmin:fedoraAdmin

Connected to the database and queried the transaction tables:

fcrepo=# select * from containment_transactions;
             fedora_id             |           parent           |     start_time      | end_time |            transa
ction_id            | operation 
-----------------------------------+----------------------------+---------------------+----------+------------------
--------------------+-----------
 info:fedora/test_container/newone | info:fedora/test_container | 2024-09-06 11:34:34 |          | 2ea259e5-c743-487
3-b1aa-dfb1a80d5105 | add
(1 row)

fcrepo=# select * from simple_search_transactions;
 id |             fedora_id             |         created         |        modified         | content_size | mime_ty
pe |            transaction_id            | operation 
----+-----------------------------------+-------------------------+-------------------------+--------------+--------
---+--------------------------------------+-----------
  3 | info:fedora/test_container/newone | 2024-09-06 11:34:33.991 | 2024-09-06 11:34:33.991 |            0 |        
   | 2ea259e5-c743-4873-b1aa-dfb1a80d5105 | add
(1 row)

I then waited for the transaction to timeout.

As described above, the entries seem to get cleared if I wait until after the Atomic Expires value returned in a GET request to the TX URI. But the amount of time before it expires seems a lot longer than the time i configured.

I tried methodically trying various conditions, but never ended up with transaction entries that stuck around forever except when I restarted fedora with transactions still live. Recording the approaches tried:

  1. Starting TX, creating a new container, then waiting 3 minutes (have it configured to 60s but it seems to be taking 3 minutes)
    • rolls back and clears DB
  2. After letting a tx roll back without restarting anything, start tx, create new container with same name, wait 3 minutes
    • rolls back and clears DB
  3. Without restarting, start tx, make GET requests against TX to check exp, create container, make GET requests against TX
    • rolls back after the updated tx exp time
  4. Create a container outside tx, make a tx, create a container in the tx (not in the outside container)
    • rolls back after the tx exp time
  5. Make a tx, create a container in a basic container that existed before the tx
    • rolls back after the tx exp time
  6. Make a tx, create a container in an existing basic container, manually roll back, make another tx, create container again
    • rolls back after about 2 minutes
  7. Make a tx, create a container in an existing basic container, shut down fedora, start fedora back up
    • tx entries still in db
    • GET for the tx returns 404, DELETE to tx returns 404
    • 7b. With tx table containing stale entry from before restart, make a tx, create a container
      • rolls back, and cleans up the new tx entries (the old ones stay)
  8. Restart postgres and fcrepo, make a tx, create a container
    • rolls back, cleans up the new tx entries
  9. Restart fcrepo (but not postgres), make a tx, create a container
    • rolls back, cleans up the new tx entries
  10. Change fcrepo timeout to 2 minutes, make a tx, create a container, GET request to check exp time
    • rolls back, cleans up tx entries after about 7-8 minutes
  11. 2 min timeout, Make tx, create container, use GET to check Atomic Expires and compare to DB
    • Atomic-Expires 19:01:01 GMT, start time in DB 14:55:16, so almost 6 minutes
    • after 2 minutes, GET to tx still says its active
    • at :01:01 mark, GET returns 410 and the db entries are gone
  12. Remove timeout config, make tx, create container
    • Atomic expires 19:13:04 GMT, start time in DB 15:04:25, so close to 7 minutes
    • GET still active after 3mins
    • Reports 410 and db entries removed after the atomic expires value

The problem with transactions after reboot is in another issue: https://fedora-repository.atlassian.net/browse/FCREPO-3952?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiM2YxYTUxZjczZTRlNDA5Mjk1NTJjNDU4ZmY5NGEwZDIiLCJwIjoiaiJ9

As for remaining transactions without restart, in our case the transaction gets stuck permanently and no rollback occurs at all. We have left the default value in the configuration. Also, I'll just explicitly point out that we're working with version 6.4 - if you were testing on 6.5, it might be different.
As for opening the transaction without further changes, I honestly don't know how it is represented. But I have tested its closure by checking that if I waited more than 3 min (approximately) after opening a transaction to send additional content, Fedora returned the information that the transaction did not exist.

If it would help, I can send some more information about our instance or the procedure, but there is nothing particularly special about them. Transactions remain stuck sometimes for a single action, sometimes for a series of actions - it doesn't seem to matter.

Hopefully this PR should either help with or resolve the issue:

https://github.com/fcrepo/fcrepo/pull/2093

The expiration times of transactions were having the timeout period added to them every request rather than being set to the now+timeout. The result was that if you made a lot of requests in a transaction, each one would add 3 minutes to the expiration time. For example, making 100 requests (read or write) gives you an expiration time 300min after the transaction was started. So it could effectively produce transactions that never seem to timeout.
